method: Every shipped gap channel in classification.json was read at the classified revision in the tool's shipped code (tests, examples, benchmarks, demos and CI scripts excluded).

confirmed: a shipped path uses the gapped capability, so the tool fails or misbehaves after the hardfork until the dependency moves; not-reached: shipped code uses the dependency only outside it; undetermined: reading cannot decide.
Each decision quotes the lines it rests on; check-leads --verify-sources re-reads every quote at its pinned revision.

Service links are decided per capability used: Ogmios chain-sync reaches block, transaction and era surfaces, submission reaches transaction and era, evaluation reaches Plutus and transaction, and the parameter query reaches protocol parameters; any read of Kupo or db-sync chain data reaches block, transaction and era (neither indexes Dijkstra blocks), db-sync parameter and pool surfaces only through epoch_param and pool tables; Blockfrost era identity only through /network/eras and parameters through the epoch parameter endpoints; Koios era identity through era fields (/tip, block and epoch info) and parameters through /epoch_params or /cli_protocol_params. Hosted Blockfrost and Koios consumers inherit the self-hosted verdicts.

gouroboros era identity and block encoding (R4 devnet) are reached when shipped code passes raw transaction bytes to DetermineTransactionType or decodes blocks or headers received from a node; building and serializing its own transactions with gouroboros types does not reach them.

Pallas era identity and block encoding (R4 devnet, 2026-10-22) are reached when shipped code decodes blocks or headers from a chain or node with MultiEraBlock or MultiEraHeader, or passes externally supplied transaction bytes to MultiEraTx::decode, which does not detect Dijkstra's three-element form; decode_for_era with an era the caller names, and Pallas primitives, addresses, keys and hashing, do not reach them.

Maestro is deprecated (2026-10-22) and will not gain Dijkstra support: any shipped call to it reaches all three provider surfaces (era identity, transactions, protocol parameters), so it is decided per tool rather than per capability; mentions in documentation, data or an unused client are not reached.
